name: BRIGHT HORIZONS FAMILY SOLUTIONS INC
business: Sells employer-sponsored early education and childcare centers, back-up care and education advisory services to employers and working families in the US, UK, Netherlands and Australia.

events.what: Compensation only: revised LTIP (more performance equity, no options), higher LTIP targets for CEO and CFO, one-time RSU for Mandy Berman (COO Back-Up Care and Ed Advisory). No change in CEO, CFO or President
events.who: Stephen Kramer, Elizabeth Boland, Mandy Berman

events.what: Director retirement, board size reduced (no addition)
CEO 'looking at strategic options' for Australia over the intermediate term (about $140M revenue, $20M to $25M annual losses); no formal review or transaction announced

next_event.source: No Investor Day or framework event found in Baba corpus. Boland: 'Step one is getting back to 10%, and then we'll be commenting later on that' (doc 112089, 2026-07-30), no date. Q3 2026 earnings date not sourced. CEO tenure: Kramer CEO effective 2018-01-01 (8-K 0001437578-17-000017).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: All numeric framing is SEGMENT adjusted operating (EBIT) margin, not consolidated EBITDA: Full Service at 5.5% in 2025, roughly stable in 2026, with a 9% to 10% long-term level (no year) built from 25 to 50 bps a year of enrollment leverage plus roughly 150 bps Australia and 50 bps closed-center drags rolling off; Back-Up Care 28% to 30% for 2026. CFO (Boland) states it, not the CEO. No consolidated margin target exists.
margin_framing.annual_bps: 25 to 50 (Full Service segment, per year, no end year)

statements.quote: If we have 150 basis points of headwind from Australia, we are able to be gaining 25-50 basis points a year, we would be adding 25-50 basis points a year as we continue to gain enrollment. ... We're well on our way to that 9%-10% with continued improvement, and we still have some centers to exit from the portfolio.
statements.speaker: Elizabeth Boland
statements.doc_title: BRIGHT HORIZONS FAMILY SOLUTIONS INC Q1 2026 Earnings Call

statements.quote: If I'm understanding your question right, it's the sort of opportunity to get back to a 10% EBIT margin, which is where we have historically operated. We certainly see a pathway to that ... Last year, we reported about 5.5% in full service. As I mentioned, we would expect it to be relatively stable with that in 2026.
statements.speaker: Elizabeth Boland
statements.doc_title: BRIGHT HORIZONS FAMILY SOLUTIONS INC Q2 2026 Earnings Call

statements.quote: We certainly see a path to getting back to 10% and honestly, beyond that. Step one is getting back to 10%, and then we'll be commenting later on that.
statements.speaker: Elizabeth Boland
statements.doc_title: BRIGHT HORIZONS FAMILY SOLUTIONS INC Q2 2026 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: Calendar fiscal year, so Baba FY labels equal company years. No target year and the target is a segment EBIT margin, so no gap is computed against consolidated EBITDA consensus. Street already models consolidated EBITDA margin rising from 16.62% (FY2025 actual) to 17.70% (FY2028), about 108 bps over three years, which is roughly the 25 to 50 bps a year Full Service rate plus Back-Up mix. The 9% to 10% Full Service level (from 5.5%) is not dated and only partly modeled.

evidence_of_progress.note: Consolidated EBITDA margin (VA actuals) Q1 2026 -45 bps YoY, Q2 2026 +95 bps YoY. Full Service adjusted operating margin Q2 2026 7.9%, +50 bps YoY, and more than +75 bps excluding Australia (Boland, doc 112089). FY2026 EPS guide raised to $5.05 to $5.15 in Q2.

disqualifier_reason: No catalyst in the 18-month window and none pending: CEO Kramer has been in the seat since 2018-01-01 and CFO Boland is unchanged; the only 2026 Item 5.02 filing is a compensation plan change; no acquisition 8-K (Items 1.01 or 2.01) since 2024-07-01; Australia 'strategic options' is informal language, not an announced review.
verdict: Very cheap and down 55%, with a CFO-stated 9% to 10% Full Service margin path, but no leadership change, no deal and no event, so there is no inflection catalyst.
open_questions: Will management exit or sell Australia, removing roughly 150 bps of Full Service margin drag?
Will the company put a year on the 9% to 10% Full Service margin, and at what event?
What explains the 41% LTM share price fall when 12-month EBITDA revisions are only -1.5%: a multiple de-rating on enrollment or Back-Up durability?
